title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Drainage Systems
description: Choosing the right pipe material for drainage, waste, and vent systems depends on acoustic requirements, fire ratings, and structural demands. Solid core PVC is lightweight, highly corrosion-resistant, and cost-effective, making it standard for residential applications. However, cast iron excels in commercial and multi-family structures due to its superior sound attenuation and non-combustible fire rating. Cast iron dramatically dampens water movement noise through walls and ceilings. Understanding the mechanical properties and code restrictions of each material ensures a durable and compliant installation.

Cast Iron vs. PVC in Drainage Systems

Choosing the right pipe material for drainage, waste, and vent systems depends on acoustic requirements, fire ratings, and structural demands. Solid core PVC is lightweight, highly corrosion-resistant, and cost-effective, making it standard for residential applications. However, cast iron excels in commercial and multi-family structures due to its superior sound attenuation and non-combustible fire rating. Cast iron dramatically dampens water movement noise through walls and ceilings. Understanding the mechanical properties and code restrictions of each material ensures a durable and compliant installation.
